the mechanism of mutagenesis by the triphosphate of this bicyclic N-4-oxydeoxycytidylate is very similar to that of the corresponding N-4-oxodeoxyguanylate.
dP is incorporated into DNA by the action of thymidine kinase, and the triphosphate is incorporated by the action of DNA polymerase into DNA opposite both G and A.

the mechanism of dP-induced mutagenesis involves the following steps: (i) phosphorylation of dC by thymidine kinase; (ii) phosphorylation of the resulting 5'-mononucleotide by nucleoside diphosphate kinase to its 5'diphosphate; and (iii) incorporation of the triphosphate of dP into the DNA by DNA polymerase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the triphosphate of a hydrogen bond ambident nucleoside deoxycytosine analog can be efficiently incorporated by DNA polymerase and is mutagenic in E.coli.
the triphosphate of a hydrogen bond ambident nucleoside deoxycytosine analog is an effective mutagen in vivo and in vitro.
dP is not only useful for in vitro mutagenic studies but also a potent mutagenic agent in vivo.
